title: Prosperity and Forgetfulness
summary: The narrator contrasts the Lord’s blessings and protection with people hardening their hearts and forgetting him amid prosperity.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord blesses and prospers those who trust in him.
The Lord prospers his people with increases in fields, flocks, herds, precious things, preservation of life, deliverance from enemies, and peace.
During prosperity, the people harden their hearts, forget the Lord, and trample underfoot the Holy One.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Fields, livestock, and precious objects may illustrate the stated prosperity; the contrast with forgetting the Lord can be conveyed through an illustrative composition.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s identities, clothing, exact setting, and specific appearance of prosperity.

narration.text: the Lord in his great infinite goodness doth bless and prosper those who put their trust in him.
then is the time that they do harden their hearts, and do forget the Lord their God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses are reflective teaching, not a narrated event at a specified time.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray a particular historical group, battle, or divine appearance.

title: Chastening and Human Pride
summary: The narrator teaches that people fail to remember the Lord without affliction, and describes their quickness to evil and pride and slowness to do good.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator says people will not remember the Lord unless he chastens them with afflictions, death, terror, famine, and pestilence.
The narrator characterizes people as quick to iniquity and pride, and slow to do good, remember the Lord, and walk in wisdom.

reasonable_visual_inferences: An illustrative contrast between worldly pride and wisdom may accompany the teaching without depicting a specific event.
unspecified_visual_details: Any particular people, calamity, or setting.

narration.text: except the Lord doth chasten his people with many afflictions
how quick to be lifted up in pride; yea, how quick to boast

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The calamities are named in a general teaching; no specific disaster is narrated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage a particular famine, pestilence, death, or terror as a present event.

title: Rejecting the Lord’s Guidance
summary: The narrator says people reject the Lord’s rule and counsel despite his goodness and mercy, and declares their nothingness.

explicit_facts.text: People do not desire the Lord to rule over them, set his counsels at naught, and refuse his guidance.
The narrator says the children of men are less than the dust of the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A visual contrast with dust may express the stated comparison figuratively.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s identities and any literal scene or setting.

narration.text: they do set at naught his counsels, and they will not that he should be their guide.
they are less than the dust of the earth.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The comparison to dust is teaching, not an instruction to depict a supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord visibly; no appearance is given.

title: Dust at God’s Command
summary: The narrator says dust moves at the command of God.

explicit_facts.text: The dust of the earth moves hither and thither and divides at God’s command.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Dust shifting and separating can illustrate the stated action.
unspecified_visual_details: The place, scale, and appearance of the dust movement.

narration.text: the dust of the earth moveth hither and thither

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes dust moving at divine command; it gives no visible appearance of God.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a divine figure or add people witnessing the movement.

title: Mountains Tremble
summary: The narrator says hills and mountains tremble at God’s voice, are broken up, and become smooth like a valley.

explicit_facts.text: Hills and mountains tremble and quake at God’s voice.
By the power of God’s voice, mountains are broken up and become smooth like a valley.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A mountain changing into a smooth valley may visualize the narrated transformation.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and appearance of the landscape.

narration.text: the hills and the mountains tremble and quake.
they are broken up, and become smooth, yea, even like unto a valley.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: God’s voice is mentioned but no visible speaker or appearance is specified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show God or add people present.

title: The Earth Shakes
summary: The narrator says God’s voice shakes the whole earth and rocks its foundations to the center.

explicit_facts.text: The whole earth shakes by the power of God’s voice.
The foundations rock to the very center by the power of God’s voice.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic cross-section of shaking ground could illustrate the stated teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific place, visible effects, and appearance of the earth’s foundations.

narration.text: by the power of his voice doth the whole earth shake;
the foundations rock, even to the very center.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: No particular earthquake or human witnesses are described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a visible divine figure or invent a specific disaster setting.

title: The Earth Moves
summary: The narrator teaches that at God’s word the earth can move or go back, lengthening the day; it appears to people that the sun stands still.

explicit_facts.text: If God says to the earth to move, it moves.
At God’s word the earth goes back, lengthening the day for many hours.
It appears to people that the sun stands still, but the earth moves and not the sun.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic view of the earth’s movement relative to the sun may represent the narrator’s explanation.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific event, location, people, and celestial appearance.

narration.text: if he say unto the earth—Move—it is moved.
it appeareth unto man that the sun standeth still;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage describes divine power in reflective narration, not a newly staged historical event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a named historical event or claim that the sun literally stops.

title: The Deep Dried Up
summary: The narrator says the waters of the great deep are dried up if God commands it.

explicit_facts.text: At God’s command, the waters of the great deep are dried up.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic contrast between water and dry ground may illustrate the statement.
unspecified_visual_details: The body of water, location, and whether this is an actual historical event.

narration.text: if he say unto the waters of the great deep—Be thou dried up—

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a conditional teaching, not a narrated historical event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a named sea crossing or add people.

title: Mountain and City
summary: The narrator gives a conditional example: at God’s command, a mountain may be raised, fall upon a city, and bury it.

explicit_facts.text: If God commands a mountain to be raised and fall upon a city, the city is buried.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic mountain above an unnamed city can convey the stated conditional example.
unspecified_visual_details: The city, mountain, people, and whether the example refers to any actual event.

narration.text: if he say unto this mountain—Be thou raised up
fall upon that city, that it be buried up

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a conditional teaching; the verse does not narrate a particular city being destroyed.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the city or depict named people or casualties.

title: Hidden Treasure Accursed
summary: The narrator teaches that treasure hidden by an iniquitous person may be cursed so no one finds it.

explicit_facts.text: Treasure hidden in the earth may be cursed because of the iniquity of the person who hid it.
If the Lord declares the treasure accursed and unfound forever, no one finds it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A concealed treasure beneath earth may illustrate the teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: The treasure’s nature, its owner, and its setting.

narration.text: if a man hide up a treasure in the earth
no man getteth it henceforth and forever.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage gives a conditional example, not a particular treasure-hiding event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a named treasure, person, or discovery attempt.

title: Consequences of Iniquity
summary: The narrator teaches that a person may be accursed or cut off from the Lord’s presence because of iniquity.

explicit_facts.text: If the Lord says a man is accursed forever because of iniquities, it shall be done.
If the Lord says a man is cut off from his presence because of iniquities, he will cause it to be so.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching may be represented symbolically without depicting divine judgment as a specific event.
unspecified_visual_details: The man’s identity, appearance, and setting.

narration.text: Because of thine iniquities thou shalt be cut off from my presence

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses are conditional teaching, not a narrated judgment scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray a named person or show the Lord’s appearance.

title: Repentance and Salvation
summary: The narrator says repentance has been declared so people may be saved, blesses those who repent and hearken, and prays that people may return to grace through repentance and good works.

explicit_facts.text: Repentance has been declared so that people might be saved.
Those who repent and hearken to the Lord will be saved.
The narrator asks God to bring people to repentance and good works and restore them to grace for grace, according to their works.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A contemplative image suggesting repentance may accompany the teaching, without specifying a particular person or event.
unspecified_visual_details: The people, setting, and visual form of repentance or grace.

narration.text: for this cause, that men might be saved, hath repentance been declared.
blessed are they who will repent and hearken unto the voice of the Lord their God;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses present general teaching and a prayer, not a specific conversion scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a conversion, divine appearance, or named repentant person.

title: The Last Day
summary: The narrator expresses the desire that all be saved, then teaches that some will be cast out, contrasting everlasting life for those who do good with damnation for those who do evil.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator wishes that all people might be saved, but says some will be cast off from the Lord’s presence in the great and last day.
The narrator says some will be consigned to endless misery and cites everlasting life for those who do good and everlasting damnation for those who do evil.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic contrast may accompany the teaching, without depicting an unmentioned judgment scene.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the last day, the people, and the manner of being cast out.

narration.text: I would that all men might be saved.
They that have done good shall have everlasting life;
they that have done evil shall have everlasting damnation.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The last day is reported in narration; the verses do not depict it as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible divine judge, heavenly figures, or a specific judgment location.
